The address follows what the panes report; on a first load and on Back or Forward it leads, restoring through the workspace port with the same command the navigator runs, once the repositories are known. It is never legacy board authority. Canonical model, scope, and checkpoint parameters describe each open pane directly, including unavailable readings. Pane closure removes those parameters. Back and reload restore them without altering legacy board command ownership. Canonical focus and hidden relationship kinds also belong to each pane address. Back, Forward, and reload restore them. Transient selection and camera state remain outside browser history. Each canonical pane also preserves diagram grammar and the explicitly selected flow. Grammar changes retain the preceding architecture scope, focus, and filters. Unavailable flow identities remain explicit. Canonical state and comparison selectors coexist with scope, focus, filters, grammar, and flow. Exact checkpoint and mutable state selection are mutually exclusive. History restores unavailable requested states without silently selecting Current. Explicit canonical addresses remain visible when the server remembers a legacy board. The existing operation owner reveals a deliberately opened legacy board. Navigation history uses the visible origin so repeated visits preserve the preview entry.

beats.title: One model, several readers
beats.narrative: The CLI, server, and browser use one canonical architecture model. The files describe modules and relationships. Each reader chooses what to show without copying that meaning.

beats.title: Open a module
beats.narrative: Opening a module changes the scope. Selection, focus, filters, and diagram grammar remain presentation choices. The local reader draws the selected architecture and keeps interaction responsive.

beats.title: Propose a change
beats.narrative: The shared runtime keeps stable identities across modules and flows. A proposal stores changed fields against an exact baseline. It does not copy the whole system into another model.

beats.title: Make the edit durable
beats.narrative: The runtime validates the complete intent and signs its checkpoint before changing current files. A journal coordinates installation and recovery. Readers hear the result only after durable completion.

beats.title: Draw the chosen reading
beats.narrative: The shared renderer measures text, lays out modules, and routes connections. The browser owns interaction. Exported pictures carry an exact recipe for the same reading.

beats.title: Explain what the reader selected
beats.narrative: The local workbench captures the exact pane reading for agent explanations and voice. Selection and focus travel with the model revision. Later navigation does not silently change that captured question.

beats.title: Keep and share exact history
beats.narrative: Adoption and shelving keep their decisions in retained history. Exact checkpoints preserve the inputs they explain. Sharing source files and publishing the architecture archive are separate actions.

issues.subject: vKEsyHFk/UOXNWLhR#3iSHwOiM
issues.mine: It writes the picture into the surface once per picture: the SVG that stays in the page under the canvas as the hidden semantic layer (picture-transition.ts). It tells the stage how the picture arrives, cut to, carried on from the last or brought in part by part, and how far the cards the two pictures share have moved; the painter does the motion. Flights read the time and their frames from the frame clock. The picture of a board that a flight into a card arrived at is put up as it is, with no entrance.
issues.theirs: It writes the picture into the surface itself, once per picture, and runs the traffic of each picture, ghost and borrowed group as it puts them up. Flights read the time and their frames from the frame clock, and the picture clock its traffic runs on is read and set through it, so a replay seeks every one of them to the frame's time. The picture of a model that a flight into a card arrived at is put up as it is, with no entrance. Continuing cards carry their one shared chip and moving words; content comparison ignores the per-picture placement properties, so a moved card keeps its shared content (picture-pairing.ts).

issues.subject: vKEsyHFk/SMjRfwN3#Kek84WN9
issues.mine:
It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, no painter is still starting, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another board, fails the render and names the frame.

A canonical talk draws its captured model and narrative through the shared walkthrough presentation. It reads no mutable vault and needs no source repository for replay.
issues.theirs:
It mounts the recording page's stage, viewer and subtitles, and no workbench, pane session or socket, so no Codex is involved. Loading a talk plays the legacy board's entrance through first, uncaptured, so frame 0 shows the legacy board at rest. A frame is ready once the fonts are loaded, no read is in flight, the step's picture is drawn and the page has not changed for two turns of its event loop, within RECORDING_FRAME_READY_MS. The stepped clock runs even the frames a library asks of the browser, and stands every animation at the frame's time, a picture's traffic at where its picture's clock stands. An animation on another timeline, or a read of another legacy board, fails the render and names the frame.

A canonical talk draws its captured model and narrative through the shared walkthrough presentation. It reads no mutable vault and needs no source repository for replay.
